questions.q: Deleting a file with Shift+Delete in Windows Explorer:
options: Deletes it permanently without moving it to Recycle Bin
questions.solution: Shift+Delete bypasses the Recycle Bin and permanently deletes the file (after confirmation). Plain Delete sends it to the Recycle Bin.
questions.shortcut: Add Shift = skip the bin. That single fact answers most Recycle-Bin questions.

questions.q: The number of layers in the OSI reference model is:
questions.solution: OSI has 7 layers (Application to Physical). The TCP/IP model that the Internet actually uses has 4.

questions.q: The hexadecimal number 2F equals which decimal number?
questions.shortcut: F=15: so 32+15 = 47. Options built from F=5, 7 or 13 are the traps.

questions.q: Which of the following is system software?
questions.solution: Windows 11 is an operating system - system software that manages the machine. PowerPoint, Photoshop and Tally are application programs that run on top of an OS.
questions.shortcut: The OS is the platform everything else installs on; look for Windows/Linux/macOS/Android among the options.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

Mumbai is the **larger** of the two megacities in terms of population.
questions.solution: **Of the two** → comparative: the **larger** of the two megacities is exactly right → No substitution required. 'Largest' needs three or more; 'more larger' doubles the marker.

questions.q: Which one of the following sentences CANNOT be changed into the passive voice?
options: The baby slept peacefully on the cot.
questions.solution: *Slept* takes no object — there is nothing to promote, so *The baby slept peacefully on the cot* has no passive at all. The other three sentences each carry an object (*a lullaby*, *the baby*, *a cradle*) and convert cleanly.
questions.shortcut: No object → no passive. Test the verb, not the looks.

questions.q: Select the correct passive form of the sentence: 'Please post this letter today itself.'
options: You are requested that post this letter today itself.
This letter is requested to post today itself.
You are requested to post this letter today itself.
You are request to post this letter today itself.
questions.solution: **You are requested to post this letter today itself.** The frame requested + to + V1 swallows the please, and the rest of the sentence is carried across word for word. A that-clause after requested is ungrammatical; making the letter the requested party scrambles the frame.
questions.shortcut: Please ... → You are requested to + V1.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the highlighted segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution required'.

The bundle of old files **were** sent to the record room.
questions.solution: The subject is **bundle**; 'of old files' is an interrupter → the bundle **was** sent. The other plural helpers repeat the illusion.
questions.shortcut: cover the 'of' phrase; bundle is singular.

questions.q: Why do steam burns cause more severe injuries than boiling water at the same temperature?
options: Steam is at a higher pressure
Steam releases extra latent heat when it condenses
questions.solution: Steam at 100 °C gives out its **latent heat of vaporisation** (about 2,260 J per gram) as it condenses on skin, in addition to the heat released by cooling. Boiling water gives only the cooling heat.

questions.q: The dry, dusty Harmattan wind, locally called 'The Doctor', blows over:
questions.solution: The **Harmattan** blows from the Sahara over **West Africa** towards the Guinea coast. Its dryness brings relief from humid heat, hence 'The Doctor'. Egypt has the Khamsin, France the Mistral and California the Santa Ana.

questions.q: Which organelle is known as the 'powerhouse of the cell'?
questions.solution: **Mitochondria** carry out aerobic respiration and produce **ATP**, the cell's energy currency — hence 'powerhouse'. Ribosomes make proteins and lysosomes are the 'suicide bags'.

questions.q: The **Hornbill Festival**, called the 'festival of festivals', is held every December in —
questions.solution: The Hornbill Festival is held from **1 to 10 December** at Kisama Heritage Village near Kohima, **Nagaland**, showcasing all Naga tribes.

questions.q: In what ratio must rice at ₹36 per kg be mixed with rice at ₹24 per kg so that the mixture costs ₹30 per kg?
The length of a rectangle increases by 20% and the breadth decreases by 10%. The percentage change in its area is:
questions.solution: $\Delta\%=20-10-\frac{20\times10}{100}=+8\%$ — an 8% increase.
questions.shortcut: $20-10-2=+8$. Traps: 10% (ignores the cross term), 'no change' (assumes cancellation).

questions.q: Which of the two numbers is greater: $\sqrt[3]{4}$ or $\sqrt[4]{6}$?
An article costing ₹1,000 is marked 25% above cost and then sold at a 15% discount. The profit earned is:

A survey of **100 people** on how they get news — Newspaper (N), TV (T) and Radio (R) — gave these region counts:

- Only N: 20 · Only T: 25 · Only R: 5
- N and T only: 15 · T and R only: 6 · N and R only: 4
- All three: 10 · None of the three: 15

How many people **read the newspaper** (with or without other sources)?
questions.solution: All four regions inside N: only N 20 + N-T 15 + N-R 4 + all three 10 = **49**. 20 is only-N; 39 forgets the all-three region.

questions.q:
**Statement:** Every customer who shops for more than ₹2,000 at a store gets a free cloth bag. Sunil got a free cloth bag from the store.

**Conclusions:**
I. Sunil shopped for more than ₹2,000.
II. A customer who shops for ₹2,500 at the store gets a free cloth bag.

Which of the conclusions follow(s) from the statement?
questions.solution: The rule says shopping above ₹2,000 is *enough* for a bag; it does not say it is the *only* way to get one, so from Sunil's bag we cannot work backwards — I **does not follow**. ₹2,500 is more than ₹2,000, so that customer is covered by 'every' — II **follows**. Answer: **only II**.
questions.shortcut: 'Every X gets Y' runs forward (X → Y), not backward (Y → X).

questions.q: Pointing to a photograph of a man, Priya said, **"He is the son of my grandfather's only son."** How is **Priya related to the man**?
questions.solution: Grandfather's only son = Priya's father; the man is his son → Priya's brother. The question asks it backwards: Priya is the man's **sister**.
questions.shortcut: Decode as usual, then flip: 'How is the speaker related to X?' wants the mirror word.

questions.q:
Three of the following four are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd one out.

**61, 67, 71, 77**
questions.solution: 61, 67 and 71 are **prime**. 77 = 7 × 11 is composite → **77**.
questions.shortcut: Numbers ending in 7 are the usual hidden multiples of 7 - test 77 first.
